items.title: Section: Five Immeasurables Open — the Boundless Realm of Beings, Worlds, Phenomena, What Is to Be Tamed, and the Means of Taming

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於五無量能起一切善巧作用。何等為五？一、有情界無量，二、世界無量，三、法界無量，四、所調伏界無量，五、調伏方便界無量。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas are able to give rise to every kind of skilful function with regard to five immeasurables. What are these five? First, the immeasurable realm of beings. Second, the immeasurable realm of worlds. Third, the immeasurable realm of phenomena. Fourth, the immeasurable realm of what is to be tamed. Fifth, the immeasurable realm of the means of taming.
Commentary: Regarding "able to give rise to every kind of skilful function" — the skilful means for maturing sentient beings number six kinds altogether, exactly as explained earlier in the chapter on the bodhisattva's own skilful means. This is what is called every kind of skilful function.

items.title: Section: The Boundless Realm of Beings, Named in Sixty-Two Kinds, and the Boundless Realm of Worlds, Illustrated by the Endurance World's Own Name

items.zh: 云何有情界無量？謂六十四諸有情眾，名有情界。如前意地已具條列。若依相續，差別無邊。云何世界無量？謂於十方無量世界、無量名號各各差別。如此世界名曰索訶，此界梵王名索訶主。如是一切皆當了知。
items.en:
What is the boundless realm of beings? It means the sixty-two classes of sentient being are called the realm of beings, exactly as already fully enumerated in the earlier Stage of Mind. Considering each being's own moment-to-moment continuity, the differences among them are boundless.
Commentary: Regarding "already fully enumerated in the earlier Stage of Mind" — sentient beings number sixty-two classes, exactly as explained in the Stage of Mind. Considering each being's own bodily continuity moment by moment, one should understand that their mutual differences are boundless.
What is the boundless realm of worlds? It means that, throughout the boundless worlds of the ten directions, boundlessly many names differ from one another. This present world, for instance, is called the Endurance World, and this world's Brahma-king is called the Lord of Endurance. All such matters should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: The Boundless Realm of Phenomena, and What Is to Be Tamed Opens With Its Simplest Classification — a Single, Undivided Kind

items.zh: 云何法界無量？謂善、不善、無記諸法，如是等類差別道理，應知無量。云何所調伏界無量？謂或有一種所調伏界。一切有情可調伏者，同一類故。
items.en:
What is the boundless realm of phenomena? It means wholesome, unwholesome, and karmically neutral phenomena. One should understand that such classifications and their distinguishing principles are boundless.
What is the boundless realm of what is to be tamed? There is, for instance, a single kind of realm of what is to be tamed — since every sentient being capable of being tamed belongs to one and the same class.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — Bound Versus Freed From Bondage, and Dull, Middling, and Sharp Faculties

items.zh: 或有二種所調伏界。一、具縛，二、不具縛。或有三種所調伏界。一、鈍根，二、中根，三、利根。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with two kinds: first, those fully bound; second, those not fully bound.
Commentary: Regarding "fully bound" and "not fully bound" — every ordinary being is called fully bound. Noble ones still in training, from the fruit of stream-entry through those on the path towards arhatship, are called not fully bound. This is as explained in the Compendium of Establishments.
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with three kinds: first, dull faculties; second, middling faculties; third, sharp faculties.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — the Four Classical Castes

items.zh: 或有四種所調伏界。一、剎帝利，二、婆羅門，三、吠舍，四、戍達羅。
items.en: There is a realm of what is to be tamed with four kinds: first, kshatriyas; second, brahmins; third, vaishyas; fourth, shudras.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — the Five Temperaments of Greed, Hatred, Delusion, Pride, and Discursive Thought

items.zh: 或有五種所調伏界。一、貪行，二、瞋行，三、癡行，四、慢行，五、尋思行。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with five kinds: first, greedy temperament; second, hateful temperament; third, deluded temperament; fourth, prideful temperament; fifth, discursive temperament.
Commentary: Regarding "five kinds of realm of what is to be tamed" — these five kinds of persons are explained at length in the Stage of Disciples; their characteristics should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — Householder and Renunciate, and Whether Wholesome Roots Have Ripened Into Liberation

items.zh: 或有六種所調伏界。一、在家，二、出家，三、未成熟，四、已成熟，五、未解脫，六、已解脫。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with six kinds: first, householders; second, renunciates; third, those not yet matured; fourth, those already matured; fifth, those not yet liberated; sixth, those already liberated.
Commentary: Regarding "householders" and "renunciates" — dwelling at home in white lay clothing, enjoying the five sensory pleasures, and managing worldly affairs to sustain one's own livelihood is called being a householder. Upholding the renunciate's own dignified bearing, abandoning worldly circumstances, upholding the precepts, and sustaining oneself purely through proper alms-seeking is called being a renunciate, as explained in the Compendium of Establishments. Not yet having gained wholesome roots sufficient to sustain the mind's continuity, unable to presently realise and see the truth, and not yet attaining the peace realised by the lesser, middle, or supreme vehicles, is called not yet matured. Its opposite is called already matured, likewise as explained in the Compendium of Establishments.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — Seven Kinds Distinguished by Attitude Towards the Teaching and Readiness for Guidance

items.zh: 或有七種所調伏界。一、輕毀，二、中庸，三、廣顯智，四、略開智，五、現所調伏，六、當所調伏，七、緣引調伏。謂遇如是如是緣，即如是如是轉變。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with seven kinds: first, the scornful; second, the neutral; third, those needing extensively displayed wisdom; fourth, those needing only briefly opened wisdom; fifth, those presently to be tamed; sixth, those to be tamed in the future; seventh, those tamed through drawing conditions.
This means that whatever condition such a being encounters, that being correspondingly transforms accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "the scornful, the neutral" and the like — beings who resent and turn against the Buddha's noble teaching are called scornful. Beings who remain neutral towards the Buddha's noble teaching are called the neutral. Those among the taught who understand only once extensively explained are called needing extensively displayed wisdom. Those who understand upon merely brief hearing are called needing only briefly opened wisdom.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — the Eight Assemblies, From Kings and Brahmins Through the Heavens of Desire and the First Dhyana

items.zh: 或有八種所調伏界。謂八部眾，從剎帝利乃至梵眾。
items.en: There is a realm of what is to be tamed with eight kinds — namely, the eight assemblies, from kshatriyas through the assembly of Brahma.

items.title: Section: What Is to Be Tamed, Continued — Nine Kinds Opens With Who Must Be Tamed by a Buddha, by a Disciple or Solitary Awakener, or by a Bodhisattva

items.zh: 或有九種所調伏界。一、如來所化，二、聲聞、獨覺所化，三、菩薩所化。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with nine kinds: first, those tamed by a tathagata; second, those tamed by a manifested disciple or solitary awakener; third, those tamed by a manifested bodhisattva.
Commentary: Regarding "those tamed by a tathagata" and the like — the Decisions section explains there are four kinds of transformative manifestation. First, manifesting bodhisattva conduct in order to bring not-yet-matured beings to maturity. Second, in order to bring already-matured beings to liberation, simultaneously and skilfully gathering them through a tathagata's own manifestation across a hundred million Jambudvipa continents within a great trichiliocosm. Third, manifesting as a disciple specifically for those beings to be transformed accordingly. Fourth, manifesting as a solitary awakener specifically for those beings to be transformed accordingly. This passage names three kinds of transformation; they should be understood according to that fuller fourfold account.

items.title: Section: The Nine Kinds Close — Hard and Easy to Tame, Gentle Words Versus Harsh Rebuke, and Distant Versus Imminent Taming

items.zh: 四、難調伏，五、易調伏，六、軟語調伏，七、訶擯調伏，八、遠調伏，九、近調伏。
items.en:
Fourth, those difficult to tame. Fifth, those easy to tame. Sixth, those tamed through gentle words. Seventh, those tamed through stern rebuke. Eighth, those tamed at a distance. Ninth, those tamed imminently.
Commentary: Regarding "tamed at a distance" and "tamed imminently" — the Stage of Disciples speaks of the distant person and the imminent person; their individual explanation there should be consulted and understood.

items.title: Section: The Tenth and Final Classification — the Ten Realms of Existence, From the Hells to Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception, Closing at Fifty-Five Total Kinds

items.zh: 或有十種所調伏界。一、那落迦，二、傍生，三、琰摩世界，四、欲界天人，五、中有，六、有色，七、無色，八、有想，九、無想，十、非想非非想。如是略說品類差別有五十五，若依相續差別道理，當知無量。
items.en:
There is a realm of what is to be tamed with ten kinds: first, hell-beings; second, animals; third, the world of Yama; fourth, gods and humans of the desire realm; fifth, intermediate-state beings; sixth, beings with form; seventh, formless beings; eighth, beings with perception; ninth, beings without perception; tenth, beings of neither perception nor non-perception.
Summarised briefly in this way, the classifications total fifty-five kinds. Considering the principle of moment-to-moment continuity, one should understand that they are truly boundless.

items.title: Section: Distinguishing the Realm of Beings From What Is to Be Tamed, and the Fifth Immeasurable, the Boundless Means of Taming

items.zh: 問：有情界無量、所調伏界無量有何差別？答：一切有情，若住種性、不住種性，無有差別，總名有情界無量；唯住種性，彼彼位轉，乃得名為所調伏界無量。云何調伏方便界無量？謂如前說，當知此中亦有無量品類差別。
items.en:
Question: What is the difference between the boundless realm of beings and the boundless realm of what is to be tamed? Answer: All sentient beings, whether abiding in a lineage or not abiding in any lineage, are without distinction gathered together and called the boundless realm of beings. Only those abiding in a lineage, progressing through their respective stages, are properly called the boundless realm of what is to be tamed.
What is the boundless realm of the means of taming? It means that, exactly as explained above, one should understand that boundlessly many distinct kinds exist here as well.
Commentary: Regarding "exactly as explained above" and the like — just as what is to be tamed, already explained above, should be understood as boundless when considered by the principle of moment-to-moment continuity, so too should this be understood here. And just as the realm of what is to be tamed has many distinct kinds, the means of taming likewise has many distinct kinds obtainable, exactly as fully set forth in the Compendium of Establishments.

items.title: Section: Why the Five Immeasurables Are Explained in This Particular Order — Closing the Fourth of the Nine Major Topics in Full

items.zh: 問：何故總說此五無量如是次第？答：以諸菩薩專精修習饒益有情，是故最初說有情界無量。是諸有情依於處所可得受化，是故第二說世界無量。是諸有情在彼彼界，由種種法或染、或淨差別可得，是故第三說法界無量。即觀如是有情界中，有諸有情有所堪任、有大勢力，堪能究竟解脫眾苦，是故第四說所調伏界無量。要由如是方便善巧，令諸有情究竟解脫，是故第五說調伏方便界無量。是故說言菩薩於此五種無量，能起一切善巧作用。
items.en:
Question: Why are these five immeasurables explained together in exactly this sequence? Answer: Since bodhisattvas devote themselves single-mindedly to cultivating the benefit of sentient beings, the boundless realm of beings is explained first. Since these very beings can only receive transformative teaching by way of the locations they depend on, the boundless realm of worlds is explained second. Since these beings, within their various realms, display distinct phenomena, whether defiled or pure, the boundless realm of phenomena is explained third. Observing that, within this very realm of beings, some beings possess the capacity and great strength genuinely able to attain final liberation from suffering, the boundless realm of what is to be tamed is explained fourth. Since only such skilful means can actually bring these beings to final liberation, the boundless realm of the means of taming is explained fifth.
For this reason, it is said that bodhisattvas, with regard to these five immeasurables, are able to give rise to every kind of skilful function.

items.title: Section: The Fruits of Teaching the True Teaching Opens — the Arising of the Teaching-Eye, and the Complete Exhaustion of Contaminants

items.zh: 諸佛菩薩為諸有情宣說正法，當知有五大果勝利。何等為五？一者、一類有情聞佛菩薩說正法時，遠塵離垢，於諸法中法眼生起；二者、一類有情聞佛菩薩說正法時，得盡諸漏；
items.en:
The buddhas and bodhisattvas, in teaching the true teaching to sentient beings, one should understand, produce five great, beneficial fruits. What are these five? First, a certain class of beings, upon hearing the true teaching taught by a buddha or bodhisattva, becomes far removed from dust and free of stain, the teaching-eye arising with respect to all phenomena.
Commentary: Regarding "far removed from dust and free of stain" and the like — the Compendium on Mutual Association explains: dust refers to the active manifestation of arrogance, whether occurring continuously or with interruption, arising from wisdom already produced but not yet complete, which obstructs direct realisation; stain refers to the coarse, latent tendencies belonging to that same category and to what is severed by the path of seeing. Since these are now eternally absent, this is called far removed from dust and free of stain. Alternatively, dust refers to arrogance together with every affliction severed by the path of seeing, while stain refers to the coarse, latent tendencies belonging to both these categories. "With respect to all phenomena" means with respect to phenomena as they abide in their own particular and shared characteristics. The teaching-eye means genuinely, directly realising wisdom that consists solely of the true teaching. This should be understood and explained accordingly.
Second, a certain class of beings, upon hearing the true teaching taught by a buddha or bodhisattva, attains the complete exhaustion of every contaminant.

items.title: Section: Arousing the Correct Vow for Awakening, and Attaining the Bodhisattva's Own Supreme Acceptance of the Teaching

items.zh: 三者、一類有情聞佛菩薩說正法時，便於無上正等菩提發正願心；四者、一類有情聞佛菩薩說正法時，證得菩薩最勝法忍；
items.en:
Third, a certain class of beings, upon hearing the true teaching taught by a buddha or bodhisattva, arouses within their own mind the correct vow towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. Fourth, a certain class of beings, upon hearing the true teaching taught by a buddha or bodhisattva, attains the bodhisattva's own supreme acceptance of the teaching.
Commentary: Regarding "attains the bodhisattva's own supreme acceptance of the teaching" — this refers to the superior-grade acceptance belonging to the stage of resolute practice, one should understand. Because one is able to penetrate that the meaning of intrinsic nature attributed to all phenomena by whatever language expresses is entirely without genuine substance, and that only the language-transcending intrinsic nature of phenomena constitutes their true meaning of intrinsic nature. Having penetrated this, there is no further meaning left to seek beyond it, which is why it is called supreme acceptance.

items.title: Section: Sustaining the True Teaching So It Endures Long Into the Future — Closing All Five Beneficial Fruits, Two Belonging to the Lesser Vehicle, Three to the Great

items.zh: 五者、一類有情聞佛菩薩說正法已，受持讀誦，修習正行，展轉方便令正法眼久住不滅。如是五種，當知名為諸佛菩薩所說正法大果勝利。
items.en:
Fifth, a certain class of beings, having heard the true teaching taught by a buddha or bodhisattva, receives it, recites it, and cultivates correct practice, and, through skilful means passed on in turn, causes the eye of the true teaching to endure for a long time without being extinguished.
These five, one should understand, are called the great, beneficial fruits of the true teaching taught by the buddhas and bodhisattvas.

blocks.text: The bodhisattva must understand five boundless things. The longest list is of beings to be tamed, classified in ten ways. It reads like a manual for a teacher meeting many kinds of students.
Beings, worlds, phenomena, those to be tamed, and the means of taming. Venerable Miào Jìng: every wise function is really encouraging beings to train in the noble path.
Venerable Miào Jìng: Sahā is usually translated "endurance": beings endure much suffering, and must endure it whether they will or not.

subs.head: Bound and free; dull and sharp

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: dull faculties can become middling, and middling sharp.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a university professor who clings to phenomena as real is of deluded temperament. Venerable Miào Jìng: a highly learned professor may still be, in Buddhist terms, deluded.

Venerable Miào Jìng: roots are ripe but liberation is not yet attained; one still needs to meet buddhas, hear the Dharma, and train. He criticises the attitude "I needn't hear the Dharma; close my eyes and I'm a buddha."

"Whatever condition is met, one transforms accordingly." Venerable Miào Jìng: meeting a teacher of the recitation method, I recite Amitābha. Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever teacher you meet, that kind of practitioner you become.

Master Cháng Bǎi recalls the old story: the washerman's son was suited to skeleton contemplation, the jeweller's son to breath counting; to those who should be saved by a buddha's form, the bodhisattva appears as a buddha.

The tenth classification includes intermediate-state beings; in all, fifty-five kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: the intermediate being is also called gandharva, "scent-seeker", seen only by the purest divine eye.
Venerable Miào Jìng: beings are primary, so they come first; without a place to live they could not be taught, so worlds come second.

Venerable Miào Jìng: "dust" is active affliction, "stain" refers to seeds; some hearers attain stream-entry. Master Cháng Bǎi: penetrating that phenomena are illusory and selfless, the dharma-eye arises. Venerable Miào Jìng adds: with hearing alone and no reflection, the dharma-eye cannot endure; you should also teach others hearing, reflection, and cultivation.
The washerman's son and the jeweller's son: each was taught through what he already knew. For anyone who teaches, this may be the most practical lesson of the day.

quiz.q: In which five immeasurables can the bodhisattva exercise every skilful function?
options: realms of beings, worlds, phenomena, those to be tamed, means of taming
quiz.why: The immeasurable realms of beings, worlds, phenomena, those to be tamed, and means of taming. Venerable Miào Jìng: every wise function is really encouraging beings to train in the noble path.

quiz.q: "This world is called Sahā" — how do the lectures explain Sahā?
options: Miào Jìng: "endurance" — enduring much suffering, enduring whether one likes it or not; Cháng Bǎi: this world is so painful that beings must endure
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: Sahā is usually translated "endurance" — beings endure much suffering, and must endure whether they will or not. Master Cháng Bǎi: because this world is painful, beings must be patient.

quiz.q: What are the "two kinds" and "three kinds" of those to be tamed?
options: fully bound, not fully bound; dull, middling, sharp faculties
quiz.why: Two kinds: fully bound and not fully bound; three kinds: dull, middling, and sharp faculties. Master Cháng Bǎi: dull faculties can become middling, middling sharp.

quiz.q: For the "deluded temperament," both lectures give the same surprising example. What is it?
options: a university professor — very learned, but grasping phenomena as real, deluded in the Buddhist sense
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a university professor who clings to phenomena as real is of deluded temperament. Venerable Miào Jìng: a highly learned professor may still be, in Buddhist terms, deluded.

quiz.q: Of the six kinds, what does Venerable Miào Jìng say about "matured but not yet liberated"?
options: roots ripe but not yet freed — still needing to meet buddhas, hear the dharma, train in the path
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: roots are ripe but liberation not yet attained — one still needs to meet buddhas, hear the dharma, and train; he criticises "I needn't hear the dharma — close my eyes and I'm a buddha."

quiz.q: For "tamed through drawing conditions," what example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: meeting a Pure Land teacher, one recites Amitābha — one turns as conditions lead
quiz.why: "Whatever condition is met, one transforms accordingly." Venerable Miào Jìng: meeting a teacher of the recitation method, I recite Amitābha. Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever teacher you meet, that kind of practitioner you become.

quiz.q: For "tamed by a tathāgata, by a disciple or solitary awakener, by a bodhisattva," what examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: teaching the washerman's son skeleton contemplation, the jeweler's son breath counting; appearing as a buddha to those tamed by a buddha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: teaching the washerman's son skeleton contemplation and the jeweler's son breath counting; to those who should be saved by a buddha's form, appearing as a buddha to teach.

quiz.q: What is the fifth of the ten kinds, and how many kinds in total are summarised?
quiz.why: Fifth, intermediate-state beings; in all, fifty-five kinds are summarised. Master Cháng Bǎi: the intermediate being is also called gandharva, "scent-seeker" — seen only by the purest divine eye.

quiz.q: Why are beings explained first, then worlds? What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: the beings themselves are primary; but without a place to live, they couldn't be taught
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: there are worlds, but the beings themselves are primary, so the realm of beings comes first; without a place to live, they couldn't be taught — hence worlds second.

quiz.q: For the first fruit — "free of dust and stain, the dharma-eye arising" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish dust and stain?
options: dust is active manifestation, stain is seeds; the dharma-eye is stream-entry
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "dust" is active manifestation, "stain" refers to seeds; some beings attain stream-entry — a great fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: penetrating that phenomena are illusory and selfless, the dharma-eye arises — the first fruit.

quiz.q: For the fifth fruit — "the dharma-eye enduring long" — what does Venerable Miào Jìng say must be done?
options: hearing without reflecting won't do; you should take students and teach them hearing, reflection, cultivation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: with hearing alone and no reflection, the dharma-eye cannot endure; you should also take disciples and teach them hearing, reflection, and cultivation.
